title: feat(console/ai): draggable chat ↔ preview split (ChatGPT/Claude-style)
body:
## Why

When the Live Canvas **preview** opens, the chat column was a fixed 42% — no way to rebalance. Continuing the "preview makes it cramped" thread (#1703), add a **draggable divider** between chat and preview, like ChatGPT's canvas / Claude's artifacts.

## What

- **Drag** the divider to resize; the width **persists** (localStorage).
- **Clamped both ways** so neither pane collapses: chat ≥ 360px, and never so wide the preview drops below 420px. A `ResizeObserver` re-clamps when the window shrinks or the chats list collapses.
- **Double-click** to reset; **←/→** resize by 24px when the divider is focused (`role="separator"`, keyboard-accessible).
- A transparent **overlay during the drag** keeps pointer events flowing past the canvas **iframe** (which would otherwise swallow them mid-drag).

Clamp logic is a pure exported `clampChatPaneWidth`; the `useResizableChatPane` hook keeps all DOM reads in handlers/effects (none during render).

## Verification

- **482/482** tests (5 new on the clamp: floor at min, cap so preview keeps room, in-range untouched, tiny-container floor wins, unmeasured container → floor only).
- `tsc` clean; no new lint errors.

Desktop-only divider (`md:block`), matching the desktop split. Pairs with the collapsible list (#1703) — together they make the preview workspace comfortable on any width.

Note: clamp + persistence are unit-tested; I haven't captured a live-rig screenshot of the drag (needs a console rebuild into the EE rig) — can do on request.
